questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) Although the monetary intervention was intended to stabilize the domestic bond market, / (2) but the unexpected escalation of international tariff disputes / (3) completely neutralized the central bank’s efforts, resulting in a sudden, / (4) sharp devaluation of the national currency.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Although the monetary intervention was intended to stabilize the domestic bond market, / (2) but the unexpected escalation of international tariff disputes / (3) completely neutralized the central bank’s efforts, resulting in a sudden, / (4) sharp devaluation of the national currency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. but the unexpected escalation of international tariff disputes .

Key Points

  • The error lies in the use of the conjunction "but" in part 2. The word "although" is already used at the beginning of the sentence, which is sufficient to indicate contrast.
  • Using both "although" and "but" in the same sentence is grammatically incorrect and redundant.
  • The correct sentence should remove "but" from part 2 to maintain proper grammatical structure.

Correct sentence: Although the monetary intervention was intended to stabilize the domestic bond market, the unexpected escalation of international tariff disputes completely neutralized the central bank’s efforts, resulting in a sudden, sharp devaluation of the national currency.

Additional Information

  • Conjunction Usage:
    • "Although" is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a contrast.
    • "But" is a coordinating conjunction used to connect two independent clauses.
    • Using both in the same clause is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
  • Tip: When "although" is used, avoid pairing it with "but" in the same sentence.

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. Hina is a best girl and knows how to manage everything.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Hina is a best girl and knows how to manage everything.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the article "a" before the superlative adjective "best."
  • Superlative adjectives (best, tallest, etc.) should be preceded by the definite article "the."
  • The correct phrase should be "Hina is the best girl," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 3 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: Hina is the best girl and knows how to manage everything.
 
Additional Information
  • Part 1: "to manage everything" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • Part 2: "No error" – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.
  • Part 4: "and knows how" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with an erroneous use of determiner in the following sentences.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the sentence with an erroneous use of determiner in the following sentences.

options.text: All I ask for is the little help from you.
options.html: All I ask for is the little help from you.

options.text: He has to take medicine every four hours.
options.html: He has to take medicine every four hours.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the determiner "the" before the term "little help."
  • When referring to a small amount of something in a general sense, the determiner "some" or "a little" should be used instead.
  • The correct phrase should be "a little help," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in Option 2 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "All I ask for is a little help from you."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "He has hardly any money." – This sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • Option 3: "He has to take medicine every four hours." – This sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • Option 4: "Any option is feasible." – This sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The international research consortium is currently consisting of twenty-five / (2) prominent evolutionary biologists representing twelve distinct academic institutions, / (3) all of whom are collaborating on a comprehensive mapping / (4) of the genetic divergence of avian species in isolated ecosystems.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) The international research consortium is currently consisting of twenty-five / (2) prominent evolutionary biologists representing twelve distinct academic institutions, / (3) all of whom are collaborating on a comprehensive mapping / (4) of the genetic divergence of avian species in isolated ecosystems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The international research consortium is currently consisting .

Key Points

  • The verb "is currently consisting" is incorrect because the verb "consist" is a stative verb and is not used in continuous tenses.
  • Stative verbs describe a state rather than an action, and they are typically used in the simple form.
  • The correct phrase should be "The international research consortium currently consists of twenty-five."

Correct sentence: The international research consortium currently consists of twenty-five prominent evolutionary biologists representing twelve distinct academic institutions, all of whom are collaborating on a comprehensive mapping of the genetic divergence of avian species in isolated ecosystems.

Additional Information

  • Stative Verbs:
    • These verbs describe states of being, thoughts, emotions, relationships, or senses rather than dynamic actions.
    • Examples: know, believe, love, hate, own, consist, seem, appear, etc.
    • They are generally not used in progressive (continuous) tenses.
  • Examples of Correct Usage:
    • Incorrect: She is knowing the answer.
    • Correct: She knows the answer.
    • Incorrect: This recipe is consisting of eggs and flour.
    • Correct: This recipe consists of eggs and flour.

The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question: One part of the sentence below may contain an error. Identify the part. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. The World Health Organisation's experts says that immunising children against the coronavirus “is not a high priority” given the extremely limited global supply of vaccines.
questions.questionHtml:
One part of the sentence below may contain an error. Identify the part. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

The World Health Organisation's experts says that immunising children against the coronavirus “is not a high priority” given the extremely limited global supply of vaccines.

options.text: The World Health Organisation's experts says that immunising
options.html: The World Health Organisation's experts says that immunising

options.text: children against the coronavirus “is not a high priority”
options.html: children against the coronavirus “is not a high priority”

options.text: given the extremely limited global supply of vaccines.
options.html: given the extremely limited global supply of vaccines.

questions.solution: The subject, "The World Health Organization's experts," is plural. The correct verb form for the plural subject should be 'say', not 'says'. The verb 'says' is used for singular third-person subjects, such as 'he', 'she', or 'it'. Therefore, the sentence should be "The World Health Organization's experts say that immunising children against the coronavirus “is not a high priority” given the extremely limited global supply of vaccines."

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. She has been speaking / four languages / very fluent / since childhood.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

She has been speaking / four languages / very fluent / since childhood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'very fluent'.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "very fluent" is incorrect in the context of this sentence. The correct form should be an adverb since it is describing the verb "speaking."
  • The correct adverbial form of "fluent" is "fluently," which modifies the verb to describe how the speaking is being done.
  • The corrected part of the sentence should read, "very fluently," to properly describe the manner in which she has been speaking the languages.

​Therefore, the correct answer is ‘Option 3’.

Correct Sentence: She has been speaking four languages very fluently since childhood.
 
Additional Information
  • "since childhood" correctly indicates the time frame since when she has had the ability to speak the languages. It is correctly used and placed at the end of the sentence.
  • "She has been speaking" is the correct use of the present perfect continuous tense, indicating an action (speaking languages) that started in the past and is still ongoing.
  • "four languages" correctly specifies the number of languages she has been speaking, fitting well into the structure of the sentence without causing any grammatical errors.

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. When I have arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

When I have arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2 i.e. (When I have arrived at)'
 Key Points
  • The correct tense to use after 'when' in this context is the simple past ('arrived'), not the present perfect ('have arrived').
  • Therefore, the sentence should read, 'When I arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.'
  • Thus, Option 2 (When I have arrived at) represents the part of the sentence with the error.
Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'When I arrived at the theatre, the show had already started.'
Additional Information
  • "had already started" - It's correctly used. When talking about two past events, the past perfect ('had started') is often used for the event that happened first.
  • "the theatre, the show" - There's no grammatical error in this part.
